input.memo_markdown:
*All data in this report is synthetic.*

## Last week's moves
First run. Nothing to review.

## What's happening
- **LinkedIn:** zero conversions since 10/18. It spent $5,249 over 14 days, and daily spend rose from ~$300 to ~$423. The prior 4-week average was 11.5 conversions per week. The cause is likely a tracking break or a delivery fault.
- **Meta:** CPA is $143.82 over the last 3 weeks vs $64.54 before, with spend flat at ~$3.4k per week. Last-click ROAS is 1.17-1.35, under the 1.5 target. Self-reported Instagram/Facebook share fell from 18% to 6%, so the decline looks real.
- **Google Search:** CPA is $17.18 over the last 3 weeks, down from $19.63. Last-click ROAS is 10-11. The September spend spike did not hurt efficiency. No action.
- **Email:** CPA is $17.66, stable, on $280 per week.
- **Direct:** conversions grew from 1.8 to 7.6 per day (4.2x) while paid spend was flat (1.03x). Self-reported AI answers (AI assistant plus ChatGPT) rose from 7% to 23%. The likely driver is AI-assistant referrals, which no paid channel should get credit for.

## Moves
- LinkedIn: $450 to $0 per day. It has had zero results for 14 days. Reversible once tracking is verified.
- Meta: $500 to $375 per day (-25%). CPA is up 2.2x on flat spend. Models still put it above target, so this is a trim and not a cut.
- Google Search and Email: unchanged.

## Where the models disagree
- Google Search ROAS ranges from 5.62 (first-touch) to 9.83 (last-touch). It is above target under every model.
- LinkedIn ROAS ranges from 0.95 (last-touch) to 2.01 (first-touch). It is above target under first-touch, linear and Markov, but the zero-conversion run is a separate problem that the models don't cover.
- Meta ROAS ranges from 2.55 to 4.09, above target under all models. These are 90-day views and miss the recent drop.
- Email ROAS ranges from 11 to 51. It is cheap, but its true value is uncertain.

## Test to run
Meta geo holdout. Pause Meta in about 20% of matched regions for 3-4 weeks. Measure total conversions and revenue across all channels, including direct. First audit the Meta pixel and creative around 9/28, when the decline began.

## Confidence
Medium overall. The LinkedIn pause is high confidence. The Meta trim is medium. I would restore Meta budget if the holdout shows a large drop in total conversions. I would revisit LinkedIn if its tracking is found broken and conversions turn out to have continued.
